```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
required_packages <- c("tidyverse", "knitr")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop("Missing package(s): ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
}

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

## User-editable settings
scamp_data_path <- "COMBINED_PIXEL_DATA_SCAMP_output.csv"
output_dir <- "Results/Threshold_validation_hom_het"
target_length <- 1000
fixed_columns <- 2
alpha <- 0.05

quantiles_to_test <- c(0.50, 0.60, 0.70)
mad_multipliers_to_test <- c(2, 3, 4)
reference_quantile <- 0.60
reference_multiplier <- 3

genotype_labels <- c("2_het" = "abcc6a+/-", "3_mut" = "abcc6a-/-")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Aim

This notebook evaluates whether the two threshold-dependent SCAMP endpoints are
robust to alternative definitions of the dataset-wide positive threshold. All
nine combinations of low-tail quantiles (50%, 60%, 70%) and MAD multipliers
(2, 3, 4) are tested. The original 60% + 3 MAD threshold is the reference.

Only positive area and mean positive fluorescence are included. Integrated
fluorescence is not evaluated because it does not depend on the threshold. This
analysis evaluates sensitivity to threshold specification; it does not provide
external biological validation of the threshold.

# Helper functions

```{r helpers}
normalize_row <- function(row, target_length = 1000) {
  row <- as.numeric(row)
  row <- row[is.finite(row)]
  if (length(row) == 0) return(rep(NA_real_, target_length))
  if (length(row) == 1) return(rep(row, target_length))
  approx(
    x = seq_along(row), y = row,
    xout = seq(1, length(row), length.out = target_length), rule = 2
  )$y
}

normalize_dataframe <- function(df, target_length = 1000, fixed_columns = 2) {
  if (ncol(df) <= fixed_columns) stop("No pixel columns were found.")
  fixed_data <- df[, seq_len(fixed_columns), drop = FALSE]
  variable_data <- df[, (fixed_columns + 1):ncol(df), drop = FALSE]
  normalized_data <- variable_data |>
    apply(1, normalize_row, target_length = target_length) |>
    t() |>
    as.data.frame()
  colnames(normalized_data) <- paste0("V", seq_len(target_length))
  cbind(fixed_data, normalized_data)
}

estimate_threshold <- function(pixel_matrix, background_quantile, multiplier) {
  values <- as.numeric(pixel_matrix)
  values <- values[is.finite(values) & values >= 0]
  if (length(values) == 0) stop("No finite, non-negative pixel values found.")
  cutoff <- unname(quantile(values, background_quantile, na.rm = TRUE))
  background <- values[values <= cutoff]
  baseline <- median(background, na.rm = TRUE)
  noise_mad <- mad(background, constant = 1.4826, na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(
    background_quantile, multiplier,
    low_tail_cutoff = cutoff,
    baseline,
    noise_mad,
    threshold = baseline + multiplier * noise_mad,
    scenario = sprintf("Q%02d_MAD%d", round(100 * background_quantile), multiplier),
    is_reference = background_quantile == reference_quantile &
      multiplier == reference_multiplier
  )
}

safe_welch <- function(data) {
  df <- data |> filter(is.finite(value), !is.na(genotype))
  if (n_distinct(df$genotype) != 2 || any(table(df$genotype) < 2)) {
    return(tibble(p_value = NA_real_,
                  mean_het = NA_real_, mean_mut = NA_real_,
                  effect_mut_minus_het = NA_real_))
  }
  mean_het <- mean(df$value[df$genotype_raw == "2_het"], na.rm = TRUE)
  mean_mut <- mean(df$value[df$genotype_raw == "3_mut"], na.rm = TRUE)
  p_value <- tryCatch(t.test(value ~ genotype, data = df,
                             var.equal = FALSE)$p.value,
                      error = function(e) NA_real_)
  tibble(p_value, mean_het, mean_mut,
         effect_mut_minus_het = mean_mut - mean_het)
}

effect_direction <- function(x, tolerance = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)) {
  case_when(
    is.na(x) ~ NA_character_,
    x > tolerance ~ "positive",
    x < -tolerance ~ "negative",
    TRUE ~ "zero"
  )
}

percent_factor_labels <- function(x) {
  paste0(as.numeric(as.character(x)) * 100, "%")
}
```

# Load and normalize the profiles

```{r load-data}
if (!file.exists(scamp_data_path)) stop("SCAMP input not found: ", scamp_data_path)
scamp_raw <- read.csv2(scamp_data_path, header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)
if (ncol(scamp_raw) <= fixed_columns) {
  stop("Expected two metadata columns followed by pixel columns.")
}

scamp_norm <- normalize_dataframe(scamp_raw, target_length, fixed_columns)
genotype_raw_all <- as.character(scamp_norm[[2]])
keep_rows <- genotype_raw_all %in% names(genotype_labels)

if (any(!keep_rows)) {
  warning(sum(!keep_rows), " row(s) with unrecognized genotype labels were excluded.")
}

pixel_data <- as.matrix(scamp_norm[keep_rows, (fixed_columns + 1):ncol(scamp_norm)])
storage.mode(pixel_data) <- "numeric"

sample_info <- tibble(
  sample_id = as.character(scamp_norm[[1]][keep_rows]),
  genotype_raw = genotype_raw_all[keep_rows],
  genotype = factor(
    genotype_raw_all[keep_rows],
    levels = names(genotype_labels), labels = unname(genotype_labels)
  )
)

if (anyDuplicated(sample_info$sample_id)) {
  warning("Sample IDs are not unique. A row identifier is used for joins.")
}
sample_info <- sample_info |> mutate(sample_row = row_number())

kable(sample_info |> count(genotype, .drop = FALSE),
      caption = "Sample counts by genotype")
```

# Threshold grid

```{r threshold-grid}
threshold_grid <- crossing(
  background_quantile = quantiles_to_test,
  multiplier = mad_multipliers_to_test
) |>
  pmap_dfr(~ estimate_threshold(pixel_data, ..1, ..2))

if (sum(threshold_grid$is_reference) != 1) stop("Reference threshold is not unique.")

write.csv2(threshold_grid, file.path(output_dir, "threshold_grid.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(threshold_grid, digits = 3, caption = "Thresholds under all scenarios")
```

```{r threshold-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
ggplot(
  threshold_grid,
  aes(factor(multiplier), threshold, colour = factor(background_quantile))
) +
  geom_line(aes(group = background_quantile)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = is_reference), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_brewer(
    palette = "Dark2",
    labels = percent_factor_labels
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 8)) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "MAD multiplier", y = "Positive threshold (a.u.)",
    colour = "Low-tail quantile", shape = "Reference"
  )
```

# Recalculate the threshold-dependent endpoints

```{r metrics}
metric_wide <- threshold_grid |>
  select(scenario, background_quantile, multiplier, threshold, is_reference) |>
  pmap_dfr(function(scenario, background_quantile, multiplier, threshold,
                    is_reference) {
    positive_area <- apply(pixel_data, 1, function(x) {
      valid <- is.finite(x)
      if (!any(valid)) return(NA_real_)
      mean(x[valid] > threshold) * 100
    })
    mean_positive <- apply(pixel_data, 1, function(x) {
      x <- x[is.finite(x) & x > threshold]
      if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else mean(x)
    })
    bind_cols(sample_info, tibble(
      scenario, background_quantile, multiplier, threshold, is_reference,
      positive_area,
      mean_positive_fluorescence = mean_positive
    ))
  })

metric_long <- metric_wide |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(positive_area, mean_positive_fluorescence),
    names_to = "metric", values_to = "value"
  )

write.csv2(metric_wide,
           file.path(output_dir, "threshold_metrics_per_sample.csv"),
           row.names = FALSE)
```

# Genotype-conclusion stability

The primary comparison from the source analysis is repeated for every threshold:
a two-sided Welch two-sample t-test comparing heterozygous and homozygous mutant
specimens. Because there is one planned genotype comparison per endpoint and
scenario, no across-scenario multiplicity adjustment is used; the scenarios are
sensitivity specifications rather than independent biological hypotheses.

```{r inference}
welch_results <- metric_long |>
  group_by(scenario, background_quantile, multiplier, threshold,
           is_reference, metric) |>
  group_modify(~ safe_welch(.x)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    direction = effect_direction(effect_mut_minus_het),
    significant = !is.na(p_value) & p_value < alpha
  )

reference_results <- welch_results |>
  filter(is_reference) |>
  select(
    metric,
    reference_effect = effect_mut_minus_het,
    reference_direction = direction,
    reference_p_value = p_value,
    reference_significant = significant
  )

stability_results <- welch_results |>
  left_join(reference_results, by = "metric") |>
  mutate(
    same_direction = direction == reference_direction,
    same_significance = significant == reference_significant,
    same_conclusion = same_direction & same_significance
  )

write.csv2(stability_results,
           file.path(output_dir, "genotype_conclusion_stability.csv"),
           row.names = FALSE)
kable(stability_results, digits = 4,
      caption = "Genotype-effect stability relative to 60% + 3 MAD")
```

# Effect-size overview

```{r effect-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ggplot(
  stability_results,
  aes(factor(multiplier), effect_mut_minus_het,
      colour = factor(background_quantile), group = background_quantile)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(shape = significant), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_brewer(
    palette = "Dark2",
    labels = percent_factor_labels
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "MAD multiplier",
    y = "abcc6a-/- minus abcc6a+/- mean",
    colour = "Low-tail quantile",
    shape = "Welch p < alpha"
  )
```

# Per-sample agreement and missing positive-pixel values

```{r agreement}
reference_values <- metric_long |>
  filter(is_reference) |>
  select(sample_row, metric, reference_value = value)

metric_agreement <- metric_long |>
  left_join(reference_values, by = c("sample_row", "metric")) |>
  group_by(scenario, background_quantile, multiplier, threshold, metric) |>
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_complete = sum(complete.cases(value, reference_value)),
    n_missing_current = sum(is.na(value)),
    spearman_rho = if (n_complete >= 3) {
      cor(value, reference_value, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
    } else NA_real_,
    median_absolute_change = if (n_complete > 0) {
      median(abs(value - reference_value), na.rm = TRUE)
    } else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write.csv2(metric_agreement,
           file.path(output_dir, "metric_agreement_with_reference.csv"),
           row.names = FALSE)
kable(metric_agreement, digits = 3,
      caption = "Per-sample agreement with the reference threshold")
```

# Interpretation guardrail

```{r interpretation, results='asis'}
non_reference <- stability_results |> filter(!is_reference)

if (nrow(non_reference) > 0 && all(non_reference$same_conclusion, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  cat("Across all tested alternative thresholds, the direction and significance classification of the genotype difference matched the 60% + 3 MAD reference for both threshold-dependent endpoints. The principal hom/het conclusions are therefore stable within the tested sensitivity range.\n")
} else {
  cat("At least one genotype conclusion changed under an alternative threshold. Inspect `genotype_conclusion_stability.csv`; a blanket claim of threshold robustness is not supported.\n")
}
```

# Important limitation

The thresholds are estimated from the complete current hom/het cohort. Their
numerical values may therefore depend on the genotype proportions and intensity
distribution of this cohort. Absolute threshold-dependent measurements from
independently processed experiments are not automatically comparable without a
harmonized threshold or external calibration.

The threshold also affects the positive regions highlighted on the ribbon plot
in the source notebook. Those highlighted regions should be treated as a
descriptive visualization based on the prespecified reference threshold, not as
an independently validated inferential endpoint.
